drivers: Recovery balance is suppressed (implied by high Z4 % and elevated aerobic TE this month vs last — 3.0 vs 2.6), ACWR likely >1.5 (this month’s 34.5 km in 7 runs vs chronic ~50–60 km/week load suggests acute spike), resting HR trend rising (avg HR up from 134 to 139 bpm), and HRV-sensitive metrics like aerobic TE and efficiency declined (efficiency worsened from 14.12 to 14.63 ml/kg/km)
readiness.guidance: This week must prioritize recovery over volume or intensity — any hard efforts risk compounding fatigue and impairing adaptation.

monthly_review.summary: Pace improved sharply (+15 sec/km faster avg) and cadence increased (+13 spm), but at the cost of higher aerobic decoupling, lower efficiency, and elevated heart rate — signs of accumulating fatigue rather than fitness gain.
monthly_review.highlight: The 16-sec/km pace improvement occurred alongside a 5-bpm HR increase, +0.4% aerobic TE, and worsening running economy — indicating compensatory effort, not sustainable efficiency gain.

goal_tracker.message: To match last month’s 51.3 km, 16.8 km across 3+ sessions would be required — but with compromised readiness, chasing this volume risks injury or burnout; recovery takes priority over numeric targets.

insights.title: Pace–HR dissociation signals fatigue, not fitness
insights.body: Despite 16 sec/km faster average pace this month, average HR rose 5 bpm and aerobic TE increased 0.4% — classic signs that the same pace now demands more cardiovascular strain, undermining endurance resilience.

insights.title: Cadence collapse on long run correlates with decoupling
insights.body: On the 10.7 km run (Sep 6), cadence dropped to 90 spm (vs monthly avg 139) while aerobic TE spiked to 5.0% — suggesting neuromuscular fatigue drove inefficient stride mechanics and compromised aerobic integrity.

insights.title: Worsening running economy tracks with reduced Z1 time
insights.body: Z1 volume fell from 43% (Aug) to 25% (Sep), while efficiency declined from 14.12 to 14.63 ml/kg/km — confirming that insufficient low-intensity recovery work is impairing metabolic efficiency.

insights.title: Z4 dominance displaces foundational zone work
insights.body: Z4 jumped from 8% (Aug) to 27% (Sep), while Z1+Z2 combined dropped from 65% to 49% — shifting training away from aerobic base building toward unsustainable stress without corresponding recovery capacity.

recommendations.action: Zone 1–2 run, HR ≤128 bpm, 45 min, Tuesday (Sep 17)
recommendations.reason: Restores Z1 volume deficit and lowers autonomic strain; HR cap set 6 bpm below last month’s avg HR (134) to ensure true recovery stimulus.

recommendations.action: Complete 20-min guided breathing session (HRV biofeedback) after waking, daily Sep 17–23
recommendations.reason: Directly targets HRV suppression — critical given compromised readiness score and elevated aerobic TE.

recommendations.action: Replace Thursday’s planned run with walk + mobility: 30 min brisk walk + 15 min hip/ankle drills
recommendations.reason: Prevents cumulative load while maintaining movement stimulus; avoids adding to acute fatigue when recovery balance is negative.

risk_flags.evidence: Aerobic TE increased from 2.6% → 3.0%, efficiency worsened (14.12 → 14.63), Z4 % doubled (8% → 27%), and avg HR rose 5 bpm despite lower volume — all converging indicators of incomplete recovery between sessions.
risk_flags.action: Cease all Z4+ efforts for 7 days; retest aerobic TE on a controlled 5 km Z2 run before reintroducing threshold work.

weekly_focus.description: Shift emphasis from pace and volume back to physiological responsiveness — using HR-controlled low-intensity work, HRV support, and movement quality to restore autonomic balance and running economy.
suggested_sessions: Recovery walk with cadence awareness (145–150 spm)
